external.description: Maryland’s communities are already feeling the impacts of climate change. Rising seas, stronger storms and heavier rainfall are increasing flood risk across the state. Flooding threatens homes, businesses, transportation networks, farms, natural areas and public safety. The Nature Conservancy is helping Maryland prepare for this future. Our goal is to make room for water and protect people by allowing nature to do what it does best. In Maryland, TNC is helping to shape state policies and programs to create sustained investments in climate resilience and adaptation. The right investments will help the state reduce flood risk in coastal and riverine communities while protecting the natural systems that people depend on. Healthy floodplains, wetlands and natural landscapes can absorb and slow floodwaters, which reduces damage to communities while providing benefits for wildlife, water quality and outdoor recreation. These nature-based solutions are among the most effective and cost-efficient ways to strengthen resilience. But making resilience a reality requires investment. According to the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, every $1 invested in resilience and disaster preparedness returns approximately $13 in avoided damages...

■コスト削減と設計思想の変化
・2足歩行を諦め台車構造を採用することで、複雑なバランス制御や駆動系機構が大幅に簡略化される。これは開発期間短縮だけでなく、製造工程における部品の精度要求を下げる効果がある。
・中国製のパーツを取り入れる「準国産」戦略は、最先端技術の獲得よりも、市場投入速度とコスト効率を優先した明確なビジネス判断である。過渡期のロボットではなく、「実用的な労働力」としての側面を強く持たせている点が重要だ。

■グローバル競争とは異なるアプローチ
